info.title: Vanshavali API
info.description: Privacy-first Indian family heritage platform. All tree data is authorised server-side.

post.description:
Always answers 202 with the same body, whether or not the email has an account (SEC-12).

A new email gets a verification link; an existing account's owner gets a notice instead.
Nobody is signed in until the link is opened (``POST /auth/verify-email``).
Consume a verification link (single use), mark the email verified and sign the user in.
Set a new password from a reset link; every session is revoked, so the user signs in again.

schema.title: Response List Sessions Api V1 Auth Sessions Get

post.description: Change the password; also the only way out of a forced change (``must_change_password``).

Close the account (PRS §54): deactivate, sign out everywhere, leave all trees.

Refused while the user is the only owner of a tree (transfer ownership or delete the tree first).
Family data the user added stays with the tree (it belongs to the family archive).

get.description: Which external sign-in options this server offers (the SPA shows only these).
Finish the Google flow: check state + nonce, exchange the code, then find/link/create the account.

post.description: Answer "this isn't me": cancel the link. No person data is read back or changed.

Answer "this is me, remove me": hide the profile now and ask a tree admin to erase it.

The link is a bearer token that may have been forwarded, so it never erases anything by itself:
hiding is immediate and reversible, erasure needs an admin (ADR-0011).

get.description:
Serve decrypted bytes for a signed, short-lived token.

The token is bound to (document, tree, user, variant, expiry). The session user must be the
user the token was issued to, and authorisation is evaluated again now, so revoked access
or a deleted document fails even while the token has not expired.
